title: Attack Path Graph
description: Optional, richer graph representation of an attack chain for the interactive HTML report. The Authorization & Attack Path Agent already emits chains as AZ-PATH-* findings with an ordered attack_path[] of step strings; the HTML report can DERIVE a linear node graph from those. This schema lets an agent OPTIONALLY supply an explicit node/edge graph (engagements/<session>/reports/attack-paths.json) when the chain is non-linear or shares nodes across paths. When present, the explicit graph is authoritative; AZ-PATH findings already represented here are not re-derived.

id.description: Stable path ID. Convention: AZ-PATH-<NNN> to align with the finding it maps to.

severity.description: Scored by end state, not the weakest step.

entry.description: Node id (or label) of the entry point.

end_state.description: Node id (or label) of the final impact/end state.

finding_id.description: The AZ-PATH-* finding this graph corresponds to, if any. Used to dedupe against derived paths.

break_chain.description: The single highest-leverage remediation that breaks this chain.

type.description: entry = attacker foothold, pivot = intermediate asset/identity, target = crown-jewel/end state, step = narrative step (used for paths derived from attack_path text).

resource_id.description: Azure resource ID this node represents, if it maps to a concrete resource. When the node also sets finding_id and that finding is aggregated (has affected_resources[]), this MUST be one of that finding's affected_resources[].resource_id — so a path traverses a SPECIFIC affected instance, not the whole rollup. See knowledge/scaling.md (Attack paths at scale).

finding_id.description: Finding that this node corresponds to (click-through target in the report). Pair with resource_id to name the specific affected instance this path step traverses.

label.description: Short technique label, e.g. 'managed identity token'.

technique.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique id, e.g. T1078.004.
